subject: radiology
title: IVC filters: indications and retrieval

steps.tx: An IVC filter earns placement only when clot protection matters and drug protection cannot work safely. **Absolute indications** centre on venous thromboembolism with **anticoagulation contraindicated** or anticoagulation that has already failed in hospital. **Relative indications** cover a massive clot burden with poor reserve and a perioperative high risk window briefly. A **prophylactic filter** without proven clot stays controversial and needs documented justification before any insertion. Ultrasound surveillance confirms caval patency before and after placement so the team deploys into a patent cava.
steps.say: A caval filter earns placement only when clot protection matters and drug protection cannot work safely. Absolute indications centre on clot disease where anticoagulation stays contraindicated or has already failed. Relative indications cover a massive clot burden with poor reserve and a perioperative window. A prophylactic filter without proven clot stays controversial and needs documented justification before insertion. Ultrasound confirms caval patency before and after placement so the team deploys safely.

steps.tx: Retrievable design beats permanent design whenever the contraindication may resolve, because dwell time creates late harm. A **retrievable filter** suits a temporary contraindication and needs active retrieval planning from the first day onward. A **permanent device** serves a lifelong contraindication or very limited life expectancy where retrieval adds only risk. **Dwell time** matters greatly because tilt, embedment and perforation rise steadily with months inside the cava. A **filter clinic** tracks every device so no filter drifts into forgotten permanence without recall attempts.
steps.say: Retrievable design beats permanent design whenever the contraindication may resolve because dwell time creates late harm. A retrievable filter suits a temporary contraindication and needs active retrieval planning from day one. A permanent device serves a lifelong contraindication or very limited life expectancy where retrieval adds risk. Dwell time matters greatly because tilt and embedment and perforation rise with months inside. A filter clinic tracks every device so no filter drifts into forgotten permanence.

steps.tx: Retrieval is a planned procedure rather than an afterthought, and imaging frames every step of removal. **Standard snare retrieval** loops the filter hook through jugular access once clot clears and drugs resume safely. **Advanced techniques** with forceps or laser sheaths free a tilted and embedded apex when snare traction fails. **Residual clot** inside the filter postpones retrieval until anticoagulation clears the trap and embolism risk falls. A **cavagram before and after** maps tilt, thrombus and caval injury across the retrieval procedure in theatre.

steps.tx: Filter complications declare through symptoms, and a forgotten device explains many late presentations in clinic. **Filter tilt with strut perforation** aches through back pain and needs urgent assessment with cross sectional imaging. **Migration toward heart or lungs** announces with chest pain and arrhythmia and needs snare rescue in expert hands. **IVC thrombosis** swells both legs and opens collaterals across the abdominal wall over time slowly. Anticoagulation resumes when possible after placement because a filter traps clot and never treats clot itself.
steps.say: Filter complications declare through symptoms and a forgotten device explains many late presentations in clinic. Tilt with strut perforation aches through back pain and needs urgent assessment with imaging. Migration toward heart or lungs announces with chest pain and arrhythmia and needs rescue. Caval thrombosis is serious because it swells both legs and opens collaterals across the abdomen. Anticoagulation resumes when possible after placement because a filter traps clot only.

steps.tx: This coronal CT shows a caval filter whose apex tilts against the wall while one strut perforates outward. The labels identify the **perforated strut**, the **IVC wall** breach and a dark **perivascular haematoma** beside the cava below. That combination explains back pain after forgotten filter dwell and warns against simple traction at retrieval. The image matters for the exam because tilt and perforation rise with dwell time inside the cava. Planned early retrieval and registry recall prevent this late complication in most patients.
